answers.rationale: Drive the full loop and claim mileage. With two material boxes and a Boise-to-Twin Falls-to-Idaho Falls sequence that can continue back to Salt Lake after Thursday lunch, driving avoids a one-way rental drop fee, airport-return constraints, and repeated material transfers. Prior Idaho planning shows the travel mode changed when material load and approved mileage made driving the lower-friction option.

Use BOS round trip with a BOS rental. Providence is close enough to Boston after a Wednesday breakfast that the one-way rental and thinner PVD-to-SLC flight inventory are not justified by the modest backtrack. The history supports choosing open-jaw only when it removes a meaningful, fragile backtrack, not as a default.

Use CLT round trip with a CLT rental. After the Asheville breakfast, the drive back to Charlotte is manageable for an evening return and preserves CLT's stronger SLC flight inventory while avoiding a one-way rental and a potentially thin AVL itinerary. Prior choices show the user favors a major-airport round trip when the smaller-airport return would add connection fragility.

Fly Tuesday morning and book Tuesday-Wednesday nights. The first assigned obligation is mid-afternoon, so a morning nonstop provides adequate buffer while avoiding an unnecessary hotel night. The history distinguishes required early or noon starts that justify arriving the prior day from agendas where a same-day early nonstop safely supports a later first commitment.
